messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: sustained high 95th pct latency and 429s on dedicated-pool-us-east-1 (customers: several enterprise tenants). Alert group: infer-runtime-high-429. Triggered at 2024-11-02T03:24Z

maria: I’m on it. escalating to page the oncall SOC. seeing a sharp qps spike to pools + queue latencies.

ajay: I’m awake, looking now. can you paste the quick pool status?

maria: running `redwoodctl pools describe dedicated-us-east-1` — past 10m: active_instances=48, queued_requests=12k, avg_token_latency=450ms, errors: 429 x3.2k, 503 x120

liam: getting the same on grafana — autoscaler trending to max but not fast enough. burst capacity flag is OFF for that pool.

maria: customer-impact: CS flagged Enterprise-A experiencing timeouts in their staging and a prod job backlog. Natalie, any inbound from CS?

natalie: yep, Enterprise-A on call. they see partial failures for batch embeddings and slow streaming. putting them on a temporary retry/backoff guidance. sending an incident note to their CSM.

ajay: quick mitigation options: 1) toggle burst (allow short-lived extra instances) 2) increase max_instances (manual scale) 3) apply temporary global rate limits to non-enterprise routes 4) route traffic to dedicated-us-west-1 fallback.

maria: what’s the risk of toggling burst? is it safe for Dedicated customers (billing/isolated capacity)?

ops-bot: Note: enabling burst will allow pool to exceed reserved capacity by up to +40% for up to 15m. Customer data still isolated. Billing will report usage as overage.

ajay: risk low for short window. but need approval to touch reserved limits and notify billing.

liam: I’m going to try burst toggle + temporary cooldown tuning. if we see 2xx return to normal, we keep for 15m then revert.
maria: ok do it. runbook steps?

ajay: Runbook extract: 
```
# enable burst
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-us-east-1 --burst true
# increase autoscaler responsiveness
redwoodctl autoscaler update dedicated-us-east-1 --scale-up-window 30s --cooldown 45s
# add temporary max_instances buffer
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-us-east-1 --max-instances 70
```
Execute in that order, monitor queue and 95th latency. If errors spike > baseline, rollback.

liam: running the burst toggle now.
liam: `> redwoodctl pools update dedicated-us-east-1 --burst true`
ops-bot: Command accepted. Pool dedicated-us-east-1 burst=true. Provisioning extra capacity (requested 18 instances).

maria: seeing new instances coming up in the cluster; queued_requests dropping from 12k -> 4k in the last 2m. 95th latency dropping to 230ms. errors 429 down to ~400.

ajay: good signal. I’m going to apply a soft global rate limit for non-critical API keys to shave tail traffic: `ratelimitctl set global --policy noncritical=50rps`

natalie: sent note to Enterprise-A: we are enabling burst capacity and rate-limiting noisy tenants; expect improved perf in ~5-10m. they acknowledged.

maria: also temporarily disabled an experimental reranker flag on canary route to reduce compute: `featurectl toggle reranker-low-latency --off`

ajay: monitoring backpressure on downstream (storage). nothing alarming.

liam: autoscaler logs show scale-up events completing, additional instances healthy.
maria: OK plan: keep burst=true for 15m, maintain increased max_instances, keep noncritical global rate-limit, keep reranker off. if stable, start revert sequence and open a postmortem.

ops-bot: Reminder: please file a billing notification ticket for overage due to burst.

natalie: CS to send customer post-incident summary after we have final numbers.

liam: handing over to day oncall @maria. brief: triggered by sudden traffic burst from a partner integration (unknown root cause), burst toggle + rate limits mitigated immediate impact, monitoring for 30m.
maria: acknowledged handoff. I’ll keep monitoring and update at 10m intervals.

(10m later)
maria: 10m check: queued_requests steady ~200, 95th latency ~210ms, errors 429 down to 40 total. Enterprise-A reports recovery.

(20m later)
maria: 20m check: stable. scheduling revert:
```
redwoodctl autoscaler update dedicated-us-east-1 --scale-up-window 60s --cooldown 120s
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-us-east-1 --max-instances 48
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-us-east-1 --burst false
featurectl toggle reranker-low-latency --on
ratelimitctl set global --policy noncritical=200rps
```
Executing revert now.

ops-bot: Revert commands accepted. Pool returning to reserved capacity.

maria: post-revert: 95th latency stable 200ms, errors ~10 last 5m.

ajay: filing incident ticket and assigning postmortem to eng-runtime. add action items: 1) tune autoscaler scale-up policy for spikes, 2) automate burst toggle when queue > threshold and notify billing automatically, 3) add per-tenant noisy-neighbor protection.

natalie: will draft external customer comms and coordinate with legal for wording if needed.

maria: marking incident as resolved. created follow-up in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (INC-2024-112). Duration: ~42m. Recommended severity: Sev2.
